messages:
samir: P0 - ACME reporting mass 400s from /v1/embeddings since ~07:12 UTC. Error text: "invalid_embedding_size". Paging @jess @lina @matt. Customer says their client expects 1536-d vectors but responses look like 1024-d. High priority, customer-facing escalation.

support-bot: New ticket created #INC-12345 (P1) — linked to this thread.

jess: reading through logs now. Any recent deploys around 07:05–07:15?

deploy-bot: canary deploy embeddings-service v2.3.1 started 07:08 UTC, completed 07:11 UTC (canary -> stable ramp 30%).

matt: hmm that timing aligns. Could be we rolled a cost-optimized variant with different embedding size. Checking model catalog and routing rules.

lina: grabbing service logs for the failing requests:

```
ERROR embeddings_service request_id=abc123 msg="invalid_embedding_size" expected=1024 got=1536 model=embed-small-q batch_id=42
WARN batching     request_id=abc123 batch_size=16 latency_ms=240 pending=3
```

lina: this shows server produced 1024 dims (embed-small-q) while ACME expects 1536. The gateway didn't validate dims and passed through the vector.

jess: so two simultaneous issues: routing returned a different model variant AND we lack a schema compatibility check at the API gateway. Quick mitigation: route ACME back to the pinned model and rollback the canary.

matt: rolling traffic back now to embed-1.4-stable for customers with pins.

```
# rollback command executed by matt
kubectl set image deployment/embeddings-service embeddings=embed-service:stable-1.4 --namespace=prod
```

alerts-bot: embeddings-service error-rate (5m) peaked 14.3% -> 1.5% after rollback.

jess: error rate trending down, latency normalizing. Support, can you confirm ACME is getting correctly sized vectors from their integration tests?

support-bot: ACME test harness reports success for 5 consecutive requests, size=1536. Customer rep says they can proceed. :thumbsup:

samir: good. Root cause hypothesis: routing policy labeled some tenant traffic as "cost_optimized" after we introduced auto-policy expansion for low-traffic tenants; that policy maps to embed-small-q (1024d). We failed to check tenant model pin before applying policy.

matt: suggested immediate follow-ups: 1) add explicit dim compatibility check in the gateway (reject with 400 + helpful message if model dim != expected), 2) change routing policy to prefer pinned model for tenants with pins, 3) add canary gating test which runs a small integration call against a sample pinned client before promotion.

jess: I'll open a PR for the gateway validation rule and schedule a quick canary test addition. Lina, can you add an alert that triggers when model variant output dims diverge from tenant expectations?

lina: on it. I'll create an alert: "embeddings.dim_mismatch.rate" and include a runbook that recommends rollback + re-route to pinned model.

support-bot: Noted: inform ACME that we found a routing regression, rolled them back, and we've got a follow-up plan. Draft message prepared for customer success.

samir: quick retrospective notes: billing impact looks limited (some failed requests), but we should check for any customers quietly retrying and incurring duplicated charges. @jess please coordinate with billing if needed.

jess: will do a scan of failed->retry patterns and correlate with recent invoices.

alerts-bot: post-mitigation check: error-rate (15m) now 0.9%, p95 latency stable.

matt: long-term remediation items I added to eng backlog: enforce model-dim as part of model metadata, blocker gating for routing policy changes, and an integration test suite that includes embedding dim checks.

samir: ACME escalation closed by customer at 07:45 UTC. Moving to postmortem, tagging oncall-sre for follow-up. Thanks everyone for quick response. :relieved:

jess: adding notes to incident board and will link PRs + test coverage.

lina: created alert + runbook, set severity to high for the first 48h, then revert to normal.

samir: closing thread — moving to postmortem doc in #incidents-postmortems.
